title: Distribution of Weekly Orders
what it shows: Histogram of num_orders, raw and after log(1 + x). Shows the target is very skewed (skew 6.9) and becomes symmetric after log.
used in report for: Data understanding - justifies training on the log scale

title: Box Plot of Weekly Orders
what it shows: Box plot of num_orders showing the long right tail; 7.2% of rows are above the 1.5 IQR limit, max 24,299.
used in report for: Data understanding - outliers and why they are kept

title: Total Weekly Orders
what it shows: Total orders per week over all centres and meals with a 10-week rolling mean. No long-term trend, spikes at week 48 and dip at week 62.
used in report for: Data understanding - trend and seasonality

title: Weekly Orders by Meal Category
what it shows: Weekly orders for Beverages, Rice Bowl, Sandwich and Other. Shows spikes come from single categories (promotions).
used in report for: Data understanding - trend and seasonality

title: Autocorrelation of Total Weekly Orders
what it shows: ACF and PACF of total weekly orders. Only a small spike at lag 1 and nothing at 52 weeks, so no yearly seasonality.
used in report for: Data understanding - seasonality / feature engineering

title: Autocorrelation per Centre-Meal Series
what it shows: Median and interquartile range of the ACF for each centre-meal series. 0.35 at lag 1 but only 0.04 at lag 10 (the forecast horizon).
used in report for: Methodology - why lags must be at least the horizon and why price/promo features matter

title: Missing Centre-Meal-Weeks
what it shows: Where the 65,017 missing rows are: 21,468 before a series starts, 40,548 gaps inside series, 3,001 after it ends.
used in report for: Data understanding / data preparation - handling of missing weeks

title: Weeks with Data for Each Series
what it shows: Map of which weeks each of the 3,597 series has a row, sorted by first week. Shows late-starting meals and gaps.
used in report for: Data understanding - missing weeks

title: Length of the Series
what it shows: Histogram of weeks per series and number of active series per week.
used in report for: Data understanding - missing weeks

title: Total Orders by Meal Category and Cuisine
what it shows: Total orders over 145 weeks by meal category and by cuisine. Beverages is the biggest category.
used in report for: Data understanding - which meals drive demand

title: Orders by Centre Type and Region
what it shows: Total orders by centre type and region code, and total orders of each centre. Type A is largest only because it has 43 centres; region 56 has about half of all orders.
used in report for: Data understanding - centre features

title: Operating Area vs Total Orders per Centre
what it shows: Scatter of centre operating area against total orders (r = 0.73).
used in report for: Data understanding - centre features

title: Price and Discount vs Orders
what it shows: Hexbin of log orders against checkout price and against discount %.
used in report for: Data understanding - price effect

title: Effect of Price Change on Orders
what it shows: Average change in log orders when a meal is cheaper or more expensive than its own average price (30% cheaper gives about +0.9 log orders).
used in report for: Data understanding / feature engineering - price features

title: Orders by Promotion Type
what it shows: Log orders for no promotion, email, homepage and both. Median orders 122, 229, 258 and 474.
used in report for: Data understanding / feature engineering - promotion flags

title: Correlation Between Numeric Features
what it shows: Pearson correlation of price, discount, promotion flags, operating area and orders. Checkout and base price are 0.95 correlated.
used in report for: Data preparation - feature selection

title: Variability of the Centre-Meal Series
what it shows: Coefficient of variation per series (median 0.63) and CV against series size. Small series are the noisiest.
used in report for: Motivation for quantile regression

title: Example Weekly Order Series
what it shows: Three example series: large and stable, medium, small and noisy (with gaps).
used in report for: Data understanding - what the series look like

title: Rolling-Origin Evaluation Folds
what it shows: Train and test weeks of the three folds: train 1-115/125/135, test the next 10 weeks.
used in report for: Methodology - evaluation / validation design

title: Correlation of History Features with Target
what it shows: Correlation of last week's orders and 4/26/all-week averages with the target for h = 1 to 10. Last week drops from 0.81 to 0.73, the 26-week average stays at about 0.84.
used in report for: Methodology - feature engineering, why longer averages are used for longer horizons

title: Baseline Error by Forecast Horizon
what it shows: WAPE of the naive, 26-week moving average and Linear Regression baselines for h = 1 to 10 (3 folds pooled). Naive rises from 34% to 55-57%, Linear Regression stays at 30-34%.
used in report for: Results - baseline performance (RQ1 reference point)

title: Model Error by Forecast Horizon
what it shows: WAPE of Linear Regression, Random Forest, XGBoost and LightGBM for h = 1 to 10 (3 folds pooled). Tree models are 2-5 points better at every horizon; error grows from about 26.5% to 31.7%.
used in report for: Results - RQ1, accuracy of tree-based models vs baseline

title: LightGBM Feature Importance
what it shows: Top 15 features by share of total gain (LightGBM, fold 3). 26-week and all-time means about 80%, then price vs usual price 4.7% and email promotion 3.7%; last week orders 0.6%.
used in report for: Results / Discussion - which inputs drive demand

title: Forecast vs Actual Orders: Centre 10, Meal 1062
what it shows: Actual weekly orders (weeks 95-145) and the 10-week forecasts of Linear Regression and LightGBM from origin week 135.
used in report for: Results - example of the forecasts

title: Pinball Loss by Quantile Level
what it shows: Mean pinball loss (3 folds) of Linear QR, quantile XGBoost, quantile LightGBM and the LightGBM point forecast for tau = 0.3 to 0.9. Quantile tree models are lowest at every level; the point forecast gets much worse at high tau.
used in report for: Results - RQ2, accuracy of the quantile forecasts

title: Coverage of the Quantile Forecasts
what it shows: % of test weeks where actual orders were below the forecast, against the target tau. All models are close to the diagonal; tree models are slightly low at 0.8-0.9.
used in report for: Results - RQ2, calibration of the quantile models

title: Quantile LightGBM Forecasts vs Actual Orders: Centre 10, Meal 1062
what it shows: Actual orders (weeks 95-145) and quantile LightGBM forecasts from origin 135: band from tau 0.3 to 0.9, lines for tau 0.5 and 0.8.
used in report for: Results - example of the quantile forecasts
